notes: Definition choice: historical NWC is computed as Total current assets minus Total current liabilities from the company’s consolidated balance sheets (this includes cash and is not explicitly debt-excluded). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))
EBIT is taken as “Income from operations” from Charter’s consolidated statements of operations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

Capex is taken as “Purchases of property, plant and equipment” from the consolidated statements of cash flows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))
WACC is sourced from StockAnalysis’s company statistics and may differ from a fully re-estimated CAPM-based WACC. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/chtr/statistics/))

Comps multiples (EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA) come from StockAnalysis and are not explicitly labeled as NTM on the pages; they are used as the closest available proxy for EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cmcsa/statistics/))

NOL balance and NOL utilization percent are not provided as explicit balances/utilization rates in the portions reviewed; set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))
Investments (as a distinct bridge line item) are not isolated in the schema-required sense from the referenced tables; set to null pending a specific investment/equity-method line-item mapping.

catalysts: Evidence of sustained customer/connectivity growth and steady operating leverage as the network evolution continues. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))

2026–2027 capex execution and any improvements in cash conversion/free cash flow versus guidance. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))
Capital allocation (buybacks/refinancings) that can change equity value even if enterprise value is range-bound.
company_overview: Charter is a leading broadband connectivity company operating primarily under the Spectrum brand, delivering Internet plus mobile, TV, and voice services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

2025 results showed modest revenue compression with stable profitability, reflecting a mature network and product mix. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity remains material: 2025 capex was $11.7B and the company guided 2026 capex to approximately $11.4B. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))
current_context: Full-year 2025 revenue was $54.8B (down 0.6% YoY) and full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was $22.7B (up 0.6% YoY). ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))

Full-year 2025 capex totaled $11.7B; full-year free cash flow was $5.0B (up from $4.3B in 2024). ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))

Company expects 2026 capex of approximately $11.4B, dependent on network evolution pace and expansion initiatives. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes low-to-mid single-digit (actually sub-1%) annual revenue growth, consistent with 2023–2025 stability/near-flat performance. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin is held near the recent range (about 0.236 in 2025) with only gradual improvement into the terminal period. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

Depreciation and amortization and capex intensity are modeled using recent run-rate percentages of sales, with 2026 capex aligned to company guidance. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))

Net working capital is negative as structured (current liabilities exceed current assets); the forecast maintains a similar negative NWC-to-sales profile. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Competitive and macro pressure could reduce revenue growth and compress margins below base-case assumptions. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))

Higher-than-modeled capex intensity or slower network evolution could reduce free cash flow durability. ([corporate.charter.com](https://corporate.charter.com/newsroom/charter-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results))

Working capital volatility could make cash flows less resilient than the negative NWC-to-sales structure suggests. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001091667/000109166726000017/chtr-20251231.htm))
Leverage/credit conditions and interest expense sensitivity could raise effective discounting and reduce valuation support.
